map.并列为三大集中趋势指标：均值受极端值影响最大，中位数只看位置，众数看频数，适合类: the median it is one of the three measures of central tendency: the mean is most affected by extremes, the median looks only at position, and the mode looks at frequency, suiting categorical or discrete data. The mode need not be unique: a maximum frequency shared by 2 values is bimodal and by 3 or more multimodal; if all values share the same frequency (including all appearing once), there is no mode. This page counts frequencies by value, with relative frequency = count ÷ valid total n × 100%, and labels unimodal/bimodal/multimodal/no mode explicitly.
map.连续型数据要先分组（如 10 岁一档），众数会随分组区间改变，不同分组不能直接比: Continuous data must be binned first (say in 10-year classes); the mode then changes with the binning and different binnings are not directly comparable. When all values are distinct there is no mode, which is not the same as "the mode is the first value". Multimodality often means two distributions were pooled (e.g. male and female heights together), so splitting before counting is more sensible. The mode is unaffected by outliers but does not reflect the overall level, so read it together with the mean/median. map.众数最适合类别型数据：服装销量最高的尺码、销量最高的车型、最常见的故障代码，这些: The mode suits categorical data best: the best-selling clothing size, the best-selling car model, the most common fault code - quantities with no meaningful "average". For numeric data the mode reflects "the most typical class", but continuous measurements almost never repeat, so the data must be binned first (say every 10 points); bin boundaries change the result and modes from different binnings are not comparable. Bimodality or multimodality usually means the sample mixes two populations - e.g. pooling the average order values of two stores - so splitting first gives a more reliable description.

map.类别数据只能看众数；数值数据若分布对称，三者接近，用均值最直观；存在极端值时中位: Categorical data can only use the mode; for symmetric numeric data the three are close and the mean is the most intuitive; with extremes the median is more robust; use the mode only when you want "the most common class".
